```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
```

## Start with a map

Pass a two-letter country code to draw one of the 202 installed maps.
Use `hc_maps()` to list every installed identifier, including regional and world maps.

```{r installed-maps}
head(hc_maps())
grep("^custom/", hc_maps(), value = TRUE)
```

For Japan, `hcmap("jp")`, `hcmap("JP")` and `hcmap("countries/jp/jp-all")`
all load the same local map.

```{r map-basics}
hcmap("jp", nullColor = "#D9E3E8", showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_title(text = "Prefectures of Japan") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

Five prefectures in the Kantō region have mountain roads featured in *Initial D*.
In Gunma, Mount Haruna is the real mountain behind Takumi’s Mount Akina.
Hover over a highlighted prefecture to see its road.
[Roads and prefectures in Initial D](https://jdmism.wordpress.com/initial-d-roads/).

```{r japan-join}
# fmt: skip
routes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~prefecture, ~road,
  "Gunma",     "Mount Haruna (Akina)",
  "Tochigi",   "Irohazaka",
  "Saitama",   "Shomaru Pass",
  "Ibaraki",   "Tsukuba Fruits Line",
  "Kanagawa",  "Hakone Turnpike"
) |> mutate(selected = 1)

kanto <- readRDS(system.file("maps", "jp.rds", package = "highcharter"))
kanto$features <- Filter(
  function(f) {
    isTRUE(f$properties$name %in% c(routes$prefecture, "Tokyo", "Chiba"))
  },
  kanto$features
)

hcmap(
  kanto,
  data = routes,
  value = "selected",
  joinBy = c("name", "prefecture"),
  nullColor = "#E3E8EC",
  dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.prefecture}")
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Initial D roads in Kantō") |>
  hc_colorAxis(minColor = "#B63848", maxColor = "#B63848", visible = FALSE) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    headerFormat = "",
    pointFormat = "<b>{point.name}</b><br>{point.road}"
  )
```

Additional boundaries can be selected by path from the
[Highcharts collection](https://code.highcharts.com/mapdata/). For a path
outside the package, the default downloads the geometry in R. With
`download_map_data = FALSE` the browser loads the map from the CDN instead.

## Income around the world

The packaged `gni2014` table contains World Bank Atlas-method income per person. Join its
three-letter country code to the map's `iso-a3` property. A logarithmic color
scale makes the differences visible across the full range of incomes.

```{r world-income}
palette <- c("#000004", "#56106E", "#BB3754", "#F98C0A", "#FCFFA4")

hcmap(
  "custom/world-robinson-lowres",
  data = gni2014,
  value = "GNI",
  joinBy = c("iso-a3", "iso3"),
  name = "GNI per capita",
  borderWidth = 0.2,
  nullColor = "#eceef2"
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Gross national income per capita, 2014") |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    type = "logarithmic",
    stops = color_stops(colors = palette)
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(valuePrefix = "$", valueDecimals = 0) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

## Map properties and joins

The join keys depend on the selected map. `get_data_from_map()` exposes those
properties. The package's local world boundaries use `iso3`; map-collection
boundaries commonly use `iso-a2`, `iso-a3` or `hc-key`.

```{r map-properties}
get_data_from_map(worldgeojson) |>
  select(any_of(c("name", "iso3", "continent"))) |>
  head()
```

To save other collection boundaries for offline use, call `download_map_data()` once and retain
the returned object with your project. Pass it as `mapData` to a map series.

```{r offline-map, eval=FALSE}
boundaries <- download_map_data("countries/us/us-ca-all")
saveRDS(boundaries, "california-counties.rds")
```

## Bring your own GeoJSON or TopoJSON

Read your file with `jsonlite::read_json()`, keeping the nested lists intact.
TopoJSON can store a shared border once for both neighbors. This example uses two
illustrative districts that share a boundary. The file ships with highcharter so
you can run the example offline. Substitute your own file path to use your map.

```{r custom-boundaries}
path <- system.file("extdata", "districts.topo.json", package = "highcharter")
districts <- jsonlite::read_json(path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
get_data_from_map(districts)
```

The map has a `code` property and the observations use `district_id`. Supply the
map key first and the table key second. Keep identifiers with leading zeros as text.

```{r custom-boundaries-join}
visits <- data.frame(district_id = c("01", "02"), visits = c(18, 42))

hcmap(
  districts,
  data = visits,
  value = "visits",
  joinBy = c("code", "district_id")
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Visits by district") |>
  hc_tooltip(pointFormat = "{point.name}: {point.value} visits")
```

For a GeoJSON FeatureCollection the same workflow applies. To draw a boundary
file on its own, pass the list directly to `hcmap()`.

```{r own-geojson, eval=FALSE}
districts <- jsonlite::read_json("districts.geojson", simplifyVector = FALSE)
names(get_data_from_map(districts))
hcmap(districts)
```

## European time zones

Categorical maps use named data classes rather than a continuous scale.
These are standard-time groups, without seasonal daylight-saving adjustments.

```{r europe-zones}
zones <- data.frame(
  # fmt: skip
  country = c("PT", "IE", "GB", "IS", "FR", "DE", "ES", "IT", "NO", "SE",
              "PL", "AT", "CH", "FI", "EE", "LV", "LT", "GR", "RO", "BG"),
  value = c(rep(0, 4), rep(1, 9), rep(2, 7))
)
hcmap(
  "custom/europe",
  data = zones,
  value = "value",
  joinBy = c("iso-a2", "country"),
  name = "Standard time",
  dataLabels = list(enabled = TRUE, format = "{point.country}")
) |>
  hc_colorAxis(
    dataClassColor = "category",
    dataClasses = list(
      list(from = 0, to = 0, name = "UTC"),
      list(from = 1, to = 1, name = "UTC + 1"),
      list(from = 2, to = 2, name = "UTC + 2")
    )
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Standard time in Europe")
```

## Airport locations

Longitude and latitude place these international airports on the basemap.

```{r airports}
# fmt: skip
airports <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,          ~lat,   ~lon,
  "Santiago",   -33.39, -70.79,
  "São Paulo",  -23.44, -46.47,
  "Bogotá",       4.70, -74.15,
  "Asunción",   -25.24, -57.52
)
south_america <- hcmap(
  "custom/south-america",
  nullColor = "#D9E3E8",
  showInLegend = FALSE
)
south_america |>
  hc_add_series(
    airports,
    type = "mappoint",
    name = "Airports",
    hcaes(lon = lon, lat = lat, name = name)
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "Airports in South America")
```

## Projection and initial view

Set a projection, center and zoom through `hc_mapView()`. Coordinates are always
longitude first and latitude second.

```{r map-view}
hcmap("custom/world.topo.json", nullColor = "#D9E3E8", showInLegend = FALSE) |>
  hc_mapView(
    projection = list(name = "Orthographic", rotation = c(65, 20))
  ) |>
  hc_title(text = "A view centered on South America") |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE)
```

## Web tiles and other geographic series

`mapline` draws boundaries, `geoheatmap` colors geographic cells and `flowmap`
connects places. The Santiago example loads Esri World Imagery satellite tiles over the internet as you pan or zoom.

```{r web-tiles}
highchart(type = "map") |>
  hc_mapView(
    projection = list(name = "WebMercator"),
    center = c(-70.67, -33.45),
    zoom = 9
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "tiledwebmap",
    name = "Santiago",
    showInLegend = FALSE,
    provider = list(type = "Esri", theme = "WorldImagery")
  ) |>
  hc_mapNavigation(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_credits(enabled = TRUE)
```

[Highcharts Maps documentation](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/maps/getting-started)
